items.title: Private Driver Pickup at Via Hotel → Shifen

tips: Give the driver the Chinese address 新北市平溪區乾坑10號; the park has a visitor centre, toilets and parking.
Nearest listed paid lot: 城市車旅平溪停三, about 526 m from the park — NT$35 first hour, then NT$15 per 30 min, NT$100 daily cap.
Arriving ~9:30 AM is after the 9:00 AM opening, so there is no wait at the gate.

items.title: Shifen Waterfall Trails & Viewpoints
items.hours: Non-summer season (Oct–May): 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:30. (Summer Jun–Sep is 09:00–18:00.)
items.getThere: Driver to 新北市平溪區乾坑10號. From the Shifen visitor centre, walk across 四廣潭橋 (Sihguangtan Bridge) toward the falls.
highlights: Shifen Falls: a curtain-type waterfall on the Keelung River main stream, nicknamed 'Taiwan's Niagara' for its resemblance; the plunge pool below is very deep.
When sun hits the spray a rainbow often appears — look from the lower platforms.
Along the walk from the visitor centre: Sihguangtan pothole formations and Yanjingdong (Spectacles Cave) Falls.
Several viewing platforms: upper ones look onto the green pool at the lip; the lower one gives the full frontal view, the classic photo spot.
tips: Budget the full 65 min: the walk out from the visitor centre plus multiple platforms takes longer than the falls alone suggest.
No sky lantern needed — the park itself is the attraction.
items.watch: Last entry 16:30 in December; irrelevant for a morning visit but matters if the day is reshuffled.

sources.label: New Taipei City Travel — Shifen Waterfall Park

items.title: Drive to Jinguashi
items.getThere: Gold Museum's official driving route: Freeway 1 toward Keelung → Dahua System IC → Prov. Hwy 62 (Wanrui Expressway) → Ruifang exit → Hwy 2丁 → right on 明燈路 → through Jiufen → North 34 (北34) → Gold Museum. In Google Maps search '黃金博物館遊客服務中心'.
tips: Parking near the museum is limited; the museum advises using the Quanji Temple (勸濟堂) car park, about a 10-min walk — also the Teapot Mountain trailhead side.
Vehicle controls with shuttle buses apply on national holidays and special-event days only; a Wednesday is normally unaffected.
The mountain road into the museum area takes about 15 min of curves; take motion-sickness precautions.

sources.label: Gold Museum — Transport (official)

items.title: Lunch in Jinguashi — Eat Before the Hike
items.hours: Miners' Cafe (礦工食堂): weekdays 09:00–17:00, weekends 09:00–18:00. Gold Museum: Mon–Fri 09:30–17:00 (Wed Dec 2 open).
items.cost: Gold Museum admission NT$80 (cash, credit card or O'Pay at the counter; online via the museum's ticket site / Taipei Fun Pass).
items.getThere: Miners' Cafe is at 新北市瑞芳區金光路8-1號 (tel 02-2496-2898), inside the Gold Museum park next to No. 8 Jinguang Rd.
highlights: Miners' Cafe is the site of the miners' lunch box (礦工便當) referenced in the notes; it also sells sweet-potato soft serve made from Tainung No. 18 sweet potato.
If time allows after eating: the museum park itself is the rain backup for the hike.
tips: Eat at the cafe, not in the museum: eating, drinking and gum are banned inside museum buildings.
Gold-panning experience was suspended Oct 5–Nov 30, 2026 for roof works; the notice runs to Dec 1, so confirm on arrival before planning around it.
items.watch: Museum closed on the first Monday of each month (Dec 7, 2026), Lunar New Year's Eve/Day and government natural-disaster closure days. Dec 2 (Wed) is not a closure day.

items.title: Teapot Mountain / Jinguashi Mining Landscape
items.getThere: Trailhead reachable from either the Gold Museum or Quanji Temple (勸濟堂); the official listing gives the route as about 1.16 km. Hiker reports: ~10 min from Quanji Temple to the trailhead, then stone steps to a mid-slope viewpoint and the 'teapot mouth'.
highlights: Teapot Mountain (無耳茶壺山), ~600 m elevation, named for its handleless-teapot summit as seen from Jinguashi.
Summit views: the Pacific to the east, Banping Mountain to the south, Keelung Mountain and the coastal road, and the blue-yellow Yin-Yang Sea below.
The 'teapot mouth' at the top: a rock opening you climb into and out the other side — the signature photo spot.
tips: Official grade: 'natural hiking' (stone and timber surfacing) with alternating climbs and flats; strenuous for unfit walkers but easy for this group.
Hiker reports put the ascent at 40–60 min and descent 30–40 min, which fits the 2-hour block with summit time.
There is no water or food on the trail; carry at least 500 ml each.
items.watch: The teapot-mouth scramble needs hands and feet; skip it if rock is wet. Steps get slippery in rain, and winter brings northeast-monsoon wind and fog — turn back at the lower viewpoint if visibility goes.

items.title: Golden Waterfall & Yin-Yang Sea (Photo Stops, If on Route)
items.getThere: Both sit on the Shuinandong coastal side reached via North 34 (北34) from the Gold Museum: Golden Waterfall is beside 金水公路; Yin-Yang Sea is just north of Shuinandong village. The museum lists Hwy 2 km 78.5 (Shuinandong car park) ↔ North 34 as its coast-side road.
highlights: Golden Waterfall: water pouring over rocks stained gold by iron-sulfide minerals leached by the area's heavy rain; the streambed is golden along the approach.
Yin-Yang Sea: a bay with a sharp blue/yellow-brown split, caused by iron hydroxide from pyrite weathering on Jinguashi Mountain.
tips: Parking: Shuinandong car park is ~133 m from the Yin-Yang Sea viewpoint; the Shuinandong visitor-centre lot is ~524 m from Golden Waterfall.
Both are drive-up photo stops; 10 minutes each is enough.
items.watch: These are downhill toward the coast from the museum, not on the direct Jinguashi→Jiufen road; adding them means a descent and climb back on North 34. Drop them first if behind schedule.

items.title: Jiufen — Hillside Lanes, Food, Views, Dusk
items.hours: Jiufen Old Street (基山街) listed hours: Mon–Thu 08:00–19:00, Fri–Sun 08:00–22:00 (Wed Dec 2: until 19:00). Sunset Dec 2 in Taipei: 5:03 PM; civil twilight ends 5:28 PM.
items.cost: Free to walk. Nearby lot 禾亭-九份礦業 (~159 m): NT$200 per entry.
items.getThere: Driver to 新北市瑞芳區基山街 (Jiufen Old Street); bus stop, toilets and parking are listed at the street.
highlights: Classic snacks named by the city: taro balls (芋圓), meatballs (肉圓) and 草仔粿 (herb rice cakes).
Shengping Theater (昇平戲院), Jiufen's first theatre, with a vintage ticket booth, old film posters and kiosk.
The film location of 'A City of Sadness'; the red lanterns and hillside lights at dusk are the main event.
tips: Sunset is 5:03 PM, after you leave at 4:00 PM, so plan on daytime sea views from the upper lanes rather than dusk.
On a weekday the street winds down at 19:00, so eat snacks early rather than saving them for after dark.

items.title: Private Driver Back to Taipei
items.getThere: Either to Via Hotel Taipei Station (台北市中正區重慶南路一段60號) or straight to the Da'an area near NARA (台北市大安區仁愛路四段345巷4弄19號), which is a 6-min walk from MRT Zhongxiao Dunhua.
tips: Dropping straight in Da'an saves a cross-city return: NARA is 6 min from Zhongxiao Dunhua and 10 min from Xinyi Anhe or Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall MRT.
If Jiufen traffic runs late, skip the hotel: NARA holds the 8:30 PM slot for only 10 minutes.

items.title: NARA Thai Massage: 120-min Traditional Bodywork
items.cost: FunNow '泰式古法舒壓按摩 120 min': from TWD 1,299 (listed TWD 1,400). Thai oil massage 120 min: from TWD 1,599. Prices vary by slot.
items.getThere: No. 19, Aly. 4, Ln. 345, Sec. 4, Ren'ai Rd., Da'an (台北市大安區仁愛路四段345巷4弄19號), beside 東區粉圓. MRT Zhongxiao Dunhua 6 min walk; Xinyi Anhe or Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall 10 min. Tel 02-2771-6692.
highlights: Package: 10-min foot bath + 110-min traditional Thai massage + snack and tea (110 min of hands-on time).
All therapists are Thai women; handmade Thai dessert after the session (limited daily; substituted if sold out).
Private rooms, shower and Wi-Fi listed; rated 4.9 on FunNow (6,800+ reviews).
tips: Book in the FunNow app/site; the earliest bookable slot is 10:00, so an 8:30 PM slot should be reserved in advance.
Tell staff about any injury or sensitive areas before starting; pressure is checked during the session per reviews.
items.watch: This package cannot specify a particular therapist or therapist gender. Arrive on time: 10-minute hold, then possible cancellation without refund.

items.title: East District Late Food & Dessert
items.hours: Eastern Ice Store 東區粉圓: open daily 11:00–23:00 (open all year).
items.cost: One flat price per bowl with up to 4 toppings — NT$70 per the most recent blog update (an older guide lists NT$60). Free self-serve ice and syrup top-ups.
items.getThere: 東區粉圓, 台北市大安區忠孝東路四段216巷38號 — right next to NARA. MRT Zhongxiao Dunhua Exit 3.
highlights: Handmade tapioca pearls plus ~30 toppings: taro, sweet-potato balls, red bean, grass jelly, tofu pudding, peanuts, aiyu jelly, coix seed.
The East District is Taipei's designated night-life hub ('五夜城'), with lanes of late eateries around Zhongxiao Dunhua.
tips: Go straight from NARA: you finish at ~10:30 PM and the shop closes at 23:00. Order by pointing at the trays; a queue moves fast.
Taro and peanut toppings are already very sweet — skip extra syrup.
items.watch: Eastern Ice closes at 23:00, so the second half of the 10:30–11:30 PM block needs another late venue; none was verified for this item.
